summary.en: Israeli artillery and airstrikes continue targeting southern Lebanese towns such as Wadi Zibqin and other border communities, while Hezbollah maintains its fire and expands its arsenal, including reported shipments and activity in Yemen. The Israeli government has redirected $90 million from border community recovery budgets to defense and is delaying completion of the Lebanon border wall, while US sanctions on Hezbollah affiliates are seen as having limited impact. Iranian forces are reported to be developing chemical weapons, and Iran’s Revolutionary Guards have been ordered to leave Beirut strongholds, indicating a shift in regional involvement. Civilian areas and health facilities in Lebanon remain under attack, and UN peacekeepers are surrounded by devastation. The conflict has caused 4,335 battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP.
summary.nb: Israelsk artilleri og luftangrep fortsetter å treffe sørlige libanesiske byer som Wadi Zibqin og andre grenseområder, mens Hizbollah opprettholder sitt skytevirke og utvider sitt arsenal, inkludert rapporterte forsendelser og aktivitet i Jemen. Den israelske regjeringen har omdisponert 90 millioner dollar fra budsjetter for gjenoppbygging av grenseområder til forsvar og forsinker ferdigstillelsen av Libanon-grenseveggen, mens amerikanske sanksjoner mot Hizbollah-tilknyttede anses ha begrenset effekt. Iranske styrker rapporteres å utvikle kjemiske våpen, og Irans revolusjonære garde har fått ordre om å forlate Beirut-styrkene, noe som indikerer et skifte i regionalt engasjement. Sivile områder og helseinstitusjoner i Libanon forblir under angrep, og FN-fredsbevarere er omringet av ødeleggelse. Konflikten har forårsaket 4 335 dødsfall i kamp i 2024, ifølge UCDP.

background.title: Hezbollah–Israel conflict (2023–present)
background.extract: An ongoing conflict between the Lebanese militant group Hezbollah and Israel began on 8 October 2023, when Hezbollah launched rockets and artillery at Israeli positions following Hamas's October 7 attacks on Israel. The conflict escalated into a prolonged exchange of bombardments, leading to extensive displacement in Israel and Lebanon. The conflict is part of the broader Middle Eastern crisis that began with Hamas's attack, with the short Israeli invasion of Lebanon in 2024 marking the largest escalation of the Hezbollah–Israel conflict since the 2006 Lebanon War. In Arabic, the conflict (2023–2024) is referred to as the "Support War" or the "Gaza Support War."
